clue.text: Get gruyere to start, before grating

indicators.note: before places the cheese's letter ahead of the grating piece
to start asks for only the opening letter of the word gruyere

parts.note: first letter of gruyere
a rasp is a coarse grating tool, or a grating sound

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: get the cheese out first, then grate it.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to understand it, as in 'I get it'.

clue.text: Clothing with split zip

parts.note: a getup is an outfit, clothing
and means with
split means leave, go

explanation.surface: An item of clothing with a broken zip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' looks like a fastener, but it means energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is energy and vigour, the same drive and enthusiasm as the answer.

clue.text: One who'll succeed in audition for show

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, the word sounds like another

parts.note: an heir is one who will succeed to a title or estate

explanation.surface: A hopeful performer auditions for a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' suggests a casting call, but it means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To air views is to show or make them public.

clue.text: Immediately aware of dubious practice of succeeding voting system

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so the second piece follows the voting system

parts.note: PR is proportional representation
to be onto someone is to be aware of their wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone instantly suspicious of a dodgy electoral method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aware of dubious practice' together means ONTO, as in 'the police are onto him'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is informal for at once, without delay.

clue.text: Rebel leader mostly harsh about our lot

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: spartan means austere, harsh
C, short for circa, means about
our lot is us

explanation.surface: A rebel chief treats his own side harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: Spartan comes from Sparta, the ancient Greek city famed for its austere way of life; C is short for circa, Latin for about.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus was the gladiator who led a slave revolt against Rome.

clue.text: Witch appearing with small goblin, before descending on ship

indicators.note: descending on means coming down on top of, so in this down entry the ship's letters go below

parts.note: an orc is a goblin-like creature
ere is an old word for before
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A witch and a goblin swoop down upon a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorceress is a female practitioner of magic, like a witch.

clue.text: A triumphant cry on clinching record

indicators.note: clinching means gripping, so the cry holds the record within

parts.note: aha is a cry of triumph or discovery
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A shout of triumph on clinching a record.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' looks like an article, but it is the definition: the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter A is spoken as this code word.

clue.text: Forty co-wrote singular novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: Forty authors co-wrote one unusual novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but it means new.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so two of them make forty.

clue.text: Valve to raise, lest endless suffering should follow

indicators.note: should follow puts the suffering piece after the others

parts.note: to cock is to raise, as in cocking an ear or eyebrow

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of lest is removed

parts.note: hell is suffering

explanation.surface: A warning to open a valve lest endless suffering follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Valve' looks like plumbing, but a valve is one half of a bivalve's shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Each hinged half of a bivalve mollusc's shell is a valve, and a cockle's is one example.

clue.text: Ride on and on at Longchamp, then start to flag

parts.note: sur is French for on; Longchamp is a racecourse in Paris

indicators.note: start to means just the opening letter of flag

parts.note: first letter of flag

explanation.surface: A jockey riding on and on at a French racecourse until the horse starts to tire.
explanation.walkthrough: Longchamp is a Paris racecourse, so the 'on' there is in French.
explanation.definitionFit: To surf is to ride on a wave, carried along on a board.

clue.text: Engine that's labouring to purr when hit in the centre

indicators.note: in the centre puts the blow right in the middle of the rearranged letters
labouring suggests the letters struggling and working themselves into a new order

parts.note: bop means hit

explanation.surface: An engine that labours rather than purrs smoothly, giving it a thump in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'labouring' rearranges TO PURR into TURROP; 'in the centre' puts BOP in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A turboprop is a jet turbine that drives a propeller, a type of aircraft engine.

clue.text: Result of police no longer getting firm backing

indicators.note: backing means the combined letters are read from the back, in reverse

parts.note: the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, was a police force replaced in 2001
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A consequence of a police force disbanded but taking support from a company.
explanation.walkthrough: RUC was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001; with CO it is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To result, as a verb, is to come about or happen, which is what occur means.

clue.text: Game in which the present holders are eliminated

definitions.text: Game in which the present holders are eliminated

parts.words: Game in which the present holders are eliminated
parts.note: a party game where whoever holds the wrapped gift when the music stops is out; 'present holders' sounds like current titleholders

explanation.walkthrough: 'present holders' reads like current champions losing their title, but the present is a wrapped gift passed around a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's party game where a wrapped package circulates and layers are unwrapped when the music stops.

clue.text: Note popped in post, one with sympathy: a nice surprise?

indicators.note: popped in means slipped inside, so the note goes into the post word

parts.note: to post is to send
re is a note of the sol-fa scale
I is the Roman numeral one
pity is sympathy

explanation.surface: A sympathetic note slipped into the post makes a pleasant surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendipity is happy chance, the pleasant discovery of something by accident.

clue.text: Mysterious lace skirts handmade originally, in extra large

indicators.note: skirts means goes round the edge of, so the lace word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to lace a drink is to spike it

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of handmade

parts.note: first letter of handmade
XL is the clothing size abbreviation for extra large

explanation.surface: Mysterious lace skirts, handmade, in a large size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lace' and 'skirts' look like fabric and garments, but lace means to spike a drink, and skirts means surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sphinx is proverbially enigmatic, so being like it means inscrutable.

clue.text: From the right forensics reveals suspected arsonist

indicators.note: from the right means the letters are read right to left
reveals means the letters sit visibly inside the word forensics

explanation.surface: Forensic evidence exposes the person thought to have started a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'forensics' sits OREN, which read backwards spells the emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Emperor Nero was rumoured to have started the Great Fire of Rome in AD 64.

clue.text: Finds out length, perhaps, and cuts it?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: takes measurements, of length for example
second meaning: is good enough, reaches the required standard

explanation.surface: A tailor measuring for a garment and then cutting the cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a tailor's steps; 'cuts it' is the idiom for being up to standard.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both taking dimensions and being adequate, as 'cuts it' means meeting expectations.

clue.text: Form of comedy duo's broadcast challenge

parts.note: stand-up is a form of comedy

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, the word sounds like another

parts.note: a duo is two

explanation.surface: A comedy duo's broadcast poses a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand up to someone is to confront or resist them.

clue.text: Sees term out — a long one

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone serving out a long term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a long one' refers back to 'term': this is a long academic term.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year academic period, longer than a usual school term.

clue.text: Biscuit that's Greek eclipsing Scandinavian one? They're the same!

indicators.note: eclipsing means covering, so the Greek letters surround the Scandinavian

parts.note: Inge is a Scandinavian personal name
snap is the call in the card game when two matching cards appear

explanation.surface: A biscuit described through a Greek outshining a Scandinavian, with an exclamation about matching.
explanation.walkthrough: Snap is a card game where players shout 'snap' when two cards match.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingersnap is a crisp ginger-flavoured cookie.

clue.text: Home cup tie?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ...-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour
second meaning: a ...-final match in a cup competition

explanation.walkthrough: 'Home cup tie' looks like a match at a team's own ground; British readers know a semi as a semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is British shorthand for a semi-detached house and also for a semi-final match.

clue.text: Coin in slot?

parts.note: a vent is a slot-like opening

explanation.surface: Putting a coin into a slot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coin' looks like money, but it means to make up a word or idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a phrase is to create it, devise it anew.

clue.text: Totally chilled, at home before ten, taking in beer and a film

parts.note: totally chilled means ice-cold

indicators.note: taking in means holding something inside, so the beer goes within
before places the home word ahead of the Roman ten

parts.note: in means at home
X is the Roman numeral for ten
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Relaxing at home before ten with a beer and a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice Cold in Alex is a 1958 British war film whose climax is a longed-for cold beer, so the surface suits it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a well-known British wartime movie set in North Africa.

clue.text: Oscar and parish priest: big rivals

parts.note: Oscar is the NATO phonetic code word for O
OS, outsize, means big

explanation.surface: Oscar and the parish priest are bitter rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppos is short for opposite numbers, counterparts or opponents.

clue.text: Yank in London's Burning

parts.note: to hitch is to yank or jerk

explanation.walkthrough: London's Burning was a British TV drama about firefighters; 'Yank' is a verb, and Cockney speakers drop initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning as a noun can be an itching or stinging sensation, or a burning desire.

clue.text: What you wouldn't expect for a quid?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an unexpected turn in a story
second meaning: a plug of tobacco, and a quid is a piece of chewing tobacco

explanation.walkthrough: 'quid' looks like a pound coin in British slang, but here it is a wad of chewing tobacco, which a twist also is.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot surprise is a twist, and twisted tobacco cut for chewing is also called a twist.

clue.text: Method of saving old dictator one's topping

parts.note: a PEP, Personal Equity Plan, was a former British tax-free savings scheme

I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A saving scheme of a former dictator's is described as first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' looks like old British slang for excellent, but it is a pizza topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy salami commonly spread on pizzas.

clue.text: I felt that discussion ultimately could get personal

parts.note: ow is the cry of someone who felt a pain

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of discussion

parts.note: last letter of discussion

explanation.surface: Someone feeling a discussion eventually became too personal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something your own is personal to you, belonging to you.

clue.text: He's poetry in motion: that's magic!

indicators.note: in motion means the letters are moving about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Praising someone whose graceful movement is poetry in motion, and calling it magic.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a conjuror's exclamation at the moment a trick is completed.

clue.text: Hammers would be present, but not always saw

definitions.text: Hammers would be present, but not always saw

parts.words: Hammers would be present, but not always saw
parts.note: the grammatical idea: the verb hammers is present, while saw can be past (of see) or present (of saw)

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a toolbox list, but hammers and saw are verbs, and the grammatical category describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Present and past are categories of verb time in grammar, and the word naming such a category is the answer.
